body:
### Environment

Node version: v24.15.0
npm version: v11.12.1
Local ESLint version: v10.2.1
Global ESLint version: N/A
Operating System: Windows 11


### What parser are you using?

Default (Espree)

### What did you do?

<details>
<summary>Configuration</summary>

```js
// eslint.config.js
module.exports = [
    {
        rules: {
            "no-unmodified-loop-condition": "error"
        }
    }
];
```
</details>

```js
function testFunction(filter) {
    let obj = { value: 1 };
    
    do {
        obj = Object.getPrototypeOf(obj);
    } while (obj && !filter);
    
    return obj;
}
```


### What did you expect to happen?

No error should be reported. 

The variable `obj` is modified inside the loop, guaranteeing that the loop is not infinite. The `!filter` variable is safely used as a constant guard. 

There is no logical difference between `obj !== filter` (which correctly reports no error because the rule parses BinaryExpressions correctly) and `obj && !filter` in terms of loop termination when one operand is modified.


### What actually happened?

The rule throws a false positive:
`error  'filter' is not modified in this loop  no-unmodified-loop-condition`

**Suspected Cause:**
It looks like `LogicalExpression` might be missing from the `GROUP_PATTERN` regex in `lib/rules/no-unmodified-loop-condition.js` (which currently handles `BinaryExpression` and `ConditionalExpression`). 

If `LogicalExpression` isn't grouped, it seems the rule evaluates the `!filter` branch in complete isolation from the modified `obj` branch, which leads to the false positive.


### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://eslint.org/play/#

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

### AI acknowledgment

- [ ] I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
- [x] (If the above is not checked) I have reviewed the AI-generated content before submitting.

### Additional comments

While looking into this locally, I noticed that the `GROUP_PATTERN` regex inside `lib/rules/no-unmodified-loop-condition.js` currently looks like this:
`/^(?:BinaryExpression|ConditionalExpression)$/u`

I suspect that adding `LogicalExpression` to this group pattern might resolve the issue. If the team agrees this is a bug and that this is the correct approach, I would be very happy to submit a Pull Request to implement the fix and add the corresponding unit tests!

labels.name: accepted

title: Bug: False positive in no-unmodified-loop-condition with LogicalExpressions (&&, ||)
